title_en: Fragments on the First and Second Epistles to the Corinthians
author: Gennadius of Constantinople
occasion: Brief exegetical notes on selected verses of 1 and 2 Corinthians, explaining Paul's use of Old Testament types and clarifying the meaning of certain terms.
argument: Gennadius explains that Paul uses the experiences of ancient Israel as types to instruct the Corinthians, showing that the cloud and the sea prefigured the grace of the Spirit and baptism. He argues that baptism has become for Christians what the sea crossing was for Israel: a defense against enemies, and that in baptism believers receive the Spirit of adoption and make covenants to live according to Christ's commandments. He distinguishes the charismatic gift of faith from the common faith of all believers, citing the Lord's saying about faith as a mustard seed. On 2 Corinthians 10:7, he instructs that the verse should be read with reproachful hypocrisy, criticizing those who judge by outward appearances rather than by the truth of works.

outline.move: Explains that Paul uses the ancient Israelites as a type to warn the Corinthians, with the cloud signifying the grace of the Spirit that shaded Israel from Egyptian harm and delivers believers from demonic evil.
Shows that Israel's passage through the sea corresponds to Christian baptism, which has become for believers a defense against their enemies.
Interprets baptism into Moses in the cloud and sea as a covenant to live by God's commandments, and distinguishes the charismatic gift of faith from common faith.
Cites the Lord's saying about faith as a mustard seed to confirm that Paul speaks of the gift of faith, not ordinary faith, and comments on 2 Corinthians 10:7 as reproachful hypocrisy.

cast.name: Paul
cast.who: The apostle, author of the epistles being commented upon.

cast.name: Moses
cast.who: Leader of Israel, through whom the law was given; Israel was baptized into him in the cloud and sea.

cast.name: The Lord
cast.who: Jesus Christ, quoted from the Gospels.

voices.speaker: The Lord (Jesus)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by 'the Lord says in the Gospels' and quoted directly.

key_terms.sense: A pattern or prefiguration in the Old Testament that corresponds to a New Testament reality.
The grace of the Holy Spirit, which delivers believers from evil.
Christian baptism, corresponding to Israel's passage through the sea.
Adoption as sons, received through the Spirit in baptism.
A spiritual gift, specifically the gift of faith distinct from common faith.
Faith; distinguished between the common faith of all believers and the charismatic gift of faith.
Feigned speech or assumption used for reproof.

scripture: The author cites 1 Corinthians and 2 Corinthians by standard numbering, and quotes the Gospels. Old Testament references are to Exodus events (cloud, sea, Moses) without explicit book citation. Psalm numbering is not used in these fragments.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is unknown.
The original addressee or audience of the commentary is not stated in the fragments.
The precise extent of the original commentary cannot be determined from these fragments.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He argues that baptism has become for Christians what the sea crossing was for Israel: a defense against enemies
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὅπερ ἐκείνοις ἡ διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης παρέσχε διάβασις, τῶν μὲν πολεμίων αὐτοὺς παντελῶς ἀπαλλάξασα, βεβαίαν δὲ αὐτοὺς τοῦ λοιποῦ τὴν ἐλευθερίαν δωρησαμένη, τοῦτο ἡμῖν πρὸς τοὺς ἡμετέρους ἐχθροὺς τὸ βάπτισμα γέγονεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: He explains that baptism has become for Christians what the sea crossing was for Israel: not merely a defense against enemies, but a complete deliverance from enemies and a gift of secure freedom; the sea crossing freed Israel from enemies and gave them stable freedom, and baptism does the same for Christians against their enemies.

_unresolved_facts.claim: in baptism believers receive the Spirit of adoption and make covenants to live according to Christ's commandments
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι τὸ τῆς υἱοθεσίας κομιζόμενοι πνεῦμα, συνθήκας καὶ ὁμολογίας τιθέμεθα τοῦ κατὰ τὰς Χριστοῦ λοιπὸν ζῆν ἐντολάς
_unresolved_facts.fix: in baptism believers receive the Spirit of adoption and make covenants and confessions to live according to Christ's commandments from then on (λοιπὸν = henceforth/from now on)

_unresolved_facts.claim: On 2 Corinthians 10:7, he instructs that the verse should be read with reproachful hypocrisy
_unresolved_facts.fix: On 2 Corinthians 10:7, he instructs that the verse should be read with reproachful personation/assumed character (ὑπόκρισιν = dramatic delivery/assumed role, not 'hypocrisy' in the moral sense); Paul speaks in a reproachful assumed character, not that the readers are hypocrites.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Shows that Israel's passage through the sea corresponds to Christian baptism, which has become for believers a defense against their enemies
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὅπερ ἐκείνοις ἡ διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης παρέσχε διάβασις, τῶν μὲν πολεμίων αὐτοὺς παντελῶς ἀπαλλάξασα, βεβαίαν δὲ αὐτοὺς τοῦ λοιποῦ τὴν ἐλευθερίαν δωρησαμένη, τοῦτο ἡμῖν πρὸς τοὺς ἡμετέρους ἐχθροὺς τὸ βάπτισμα γέγονεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Shows that Israel's passage through the sea corresponds to Christian baptism, which has become for believers what the sea was for Israel: complete deliverance from enemies and the gift of secure, lasting freedom

_unresolved_facts.claim: Interprets baptism into Moses in the cloud and sea as a covenant to live by God's commandments
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καθάπερ ἐκεῖνοι τούτων τυχόντες ὑπέσχοντο τοῖς Μωϋσαικοῖς νόμοις βιοῦν, οὕτω καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι... συνθήκας καὶ ὁμολογίας τιθέμεθα τοῦ κατὰ τὰς Χριστοῦ λοιπὸν ζῆν ἐντολάς
_unresolved_facts.fix: Interprets baptism into Moses in the cloud and sea as a covenant to live by Moses's laws (for Israel) and by Christ's commandments (for Christians), not 'God's commandments' generally

_unresolved_facts.claim: comments on 2 Corinthians 10:7 as reproachful hypocrisy
_unresolved_facts.fix: comments on 2 Corinthians 10:7 as requiring reproachful dramatic personation/assumed character in reading

_unresolved_facts.claim: Paul... The apostle, author of the epistles being commented upon
_unresolved_facts.fix: Paul is not explicitly named in these fragments; the commentary refers to 'he' (Paul) implicitly but never names him directly

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Lord (Jesus)... Introduced by 'the Lord says in the Gospels' and quoted directly
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: περὶ τούτου καὶ ὁ κύριος 419 ἐν Εὐαγγελίοις φησίν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Lord (Jesus)... Introduced by 'the Lord in the Gospels says' (περὶ τούτου καὶ ὁ κύριος ἐν Εὐαγγελίοις φησίν), with the quotation following but the direct quotation mark not explicitly present in the fragment as preserved
